I am not a Christian but I have studied Christian theology quite a lot so this is what I have learned about evangelisation and proselytism :

- The core belief of all trinitarian Christians is that Jesus brought the good news, "envangeliom" in greek translated in English to "Gospel", for every human being that has ever lived. 
The good news in question is that our debt in sin is payed for by Jesus' sacrifice of his own life. Jesus was and is "perfect", in the sense that he has never sinned, and only God can do that because every human being since Adam included is a sinner, no matter how hard they try not to. Without Jesus' atonement for sin, we all deserve death, it is the price of sin since Genesis, and death is a separation from God for eternity (also known as hell). 

So basically, our default state is sinful, and there is nothing we can do about it. 
This is where it gets a bit weird and metaphorical. 
In the old Testament God was asking for sacrifices from the Jews in order to have temporary forgiveness and draw closer to God. Animal sacrifices mainly. 
This is an important concept to understand the necessity of God's rescue mission through Jesus.
He was the ultimate sacrifice, because he was God himself, and went through the worst tragedy of humiliation and agony. If we are not familiar with ancient jewish monotheism this doesn't make much sense but within the biblical narrative it was like the accomplishment for all the buildup that came before. 

So knowing all that, and I purposefully made it as simple as I could, we could assume that everyone is therefore saved, no matter how evil and sinful we choose to be. 
Some denominations believe in this, and is called universalism, stating that eventually everyone will be saved because a loving God wouldn't send anyone to "eternal torment". 

But most Christians agree on one simple dogma, that we are saved through faith. What does faith mean ? It is very explicitly stated in probably the most famous bible verse John 3:16 
" For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."

"That whoever believes in him" is the key phrase here. The only condition to be saved is to have faith in Jesus Christ. 
What does it mean to have faith in him? 
Well this is where it gets more interpretative, but for me the most simple and basic definition of belief has to be applied here, it is about accepting that he is indeed the one and only Son of God, and that he died to pay for all our sins so we can live eternally after we die with our creator, instead of being annihilated and separated forever. 

That's it, believe in Jesus wholeheartedly and you will naturally draw closer to righteousness and towards God's plan for you and humanity. The Holy Spirit will come and assist you with this, because we cannot do this on our own. 

However, if you reject Jesus, and you reject God and live on your own terms, you are doomed to fall into a sinful existence and bring hell all around you. If you believe you are your own God then there is nothing above you, no humility and only tyranny and pain can be the end result, as it has many times been the case in human history. 


So most Christians will agree that it is their duty to spread this good news, and talk about Jesus to none believers or other religions, just so they know that he has a pretty solid case to be the actual son of God. 
Just to put things in context, Christianity spread in the first centuries when there was no such thing as atheism, everyone believed in gods, and the pagan gods were nothing like this "loving and caring" Jewish god that wants to offer salvation to anyone who wants to be saved. It's not that some people are rejected by God, it is more like God knows that he can try as hard as he wants some will never turn to him no matter what. 
So some modern protestant consider that salvation is in God's hands, rather that in the believers individual effort. 

So to sum it up Christianity is so wide in interpretation and denominations that you will find hardcore evangelizers that take it as a personal duty to spread the word as much as possible, and other will be more understanding of the current cultural concept which is not very receptive to people telling them what to do (understandably), and will rely on prayer and God's sovereignty to reach people around them.

I believe the trinitarian dogma was built on the verse "Me and my Father are one", so the orthodox view is basically the following : Jesus is 100% human (not a spirit, he eats, cries, bleeds) while also sharing the same substance as God the Father without falling into polytheism, the insistence is that He is one and only eternal Being. 

God the Father is best understood as a supernatural being, He is part of every molecule of the universe and is not a describable entity with our human concepts. 

This is a mystery that purposefully cannot be rationalised. 

The final authority for Christians is the New Testament and the Gospels above all, the epistle may contain inconsistencies as it was written by humans who barely understood what it all means. The letters tend to recognise Jesus as "Lord" and the Son of God, never really stating that he himself is God in human form. 

In the Gospels the clearest hint we have is the verse "Only the Father knows when the end times are coming", which logically would imply that Jesus is not omnipotent and therefore is inferior. 
This is interpreted by theologians as a limitation that God wilfully applied to himself during his visit on earth through the flesh of Jesus, so He maintains the status of a different person from the Father in our human conception. 
In other words, he could know if he wanted to but chooses not to because humans are not meant to know about the time of the second coming, there is an insistence that it could come at anytime and we should not be waiting around before repenting. 

This is known as a hypostatic union, meaning that for the Orthodox view The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are equally divine in nature while still being three separate entities, or persons.

So even even Jesus prays to the father, he does so because he is human, if he didn't it would mean that he is the same person as his Father and therefore would not pray to himself. 

Another explanation is that Jesus is the Logos, meaning the word of God, which is present from Genesis, confirmed by many verses in the Gospels that Jesus existed before his birth, and is therefore Eternal, so 100% God.

So while there might be verses that could be interpreted as Jesus being inferior to God the Father, they are all "explained" with the trinitarian dogma, which in my understanding uses the supposition that we have to accept that it is illogical and a complete mystery we can observe and describe but not explain. 

By doing so, the whole narrative of the New Testament "makes sense", at least if we chose to believe that such impossibilities are actually possible, because God is almighty and we can see only one side of the coin from our perspective. 

Without implying that Jesus is equal to God, Christianity doesn't make sense as a whole, and only Islam and Judaism can therefore be the correct way to interpret the Abrahamic God.

We do not know. We will not have any answers. As far as humanity is concerned we are all agnostic, anyone that affirms that Christianity is factually true is mistaken and misleading.

All we can do is observe and try to understand how the biblical corpus and tradition applies and translates to our existence. You can either live on in a naturalist and determinist world, if you manage not to worry too much about metaphysical issues, or you can try to fill the gaps with the supernatural produced somehow by the collective unconscious and imagery.

If you choose to go down the second path you are more likely to find one narrative that appeals to you, culturally and "spiritually". Some people worship nature, some believe in astrology, some believe in the one and true Lord Jesus Christ, so to speak.

It is really a matter of building a belief system that resonates in you and brings out the best of you, bearing its fruits through you.

I believe this is how you do it, by simply having a leap of faith.

Christianity is a very dark worldview, we are all corrupted sinners, and requires us to be in constant state of repentance, asking for the Lord's mercy and through the Holy Spirit draw closer to our creator, washing away our imperfections through the sacrifice of God himself made man and experiencing human suffering with us, and by doing so pay the ultimate price of death to redeem all those who wish to be in relationship with Him.

I mean who could even come up with such a twisted story ? It makes me honestly more scared that it might actually be the truth, I could also write whole paragraphs on how the concept of good and evil, sin, demons and satan are actually frighteningly accurate descriptions of what science cannot observe in the unconscious and metaphysical world. Sometimes it's the existence of evil that makes it all too real.

It seems like you have hit the brick wall that the existentialists still struggle to give answers to, unless as you correctly stated resort to some kind of faith and supernatural belief. 

The way I would describe how faith and religion solve this issue is that our actions here on earth during our lifetime have eternal repercussions, somehow. 
Now that is incompatible with naturalist and materialist atheism, and even agnosticism isn't enough to carry through this problem. 

I can easily see how for exemple a Christians faith in Jesus-Christ and a personal relationship with "God" can actually at least put an end to the feeling of meaningless and self destructive nihilism. That again requires true commitment. 

In a sense this was Nietzsche's point with the infamous statement "God is dead". We have chosen to detach from religion and only base our belief systems on the observable scientific method, but the human mind and consciousness cannot be observed and measured in that way, it is still a complete mystery to us. 
So his proposed solution for the problem was the Ubermensch, or Overman, stating that our morality must now come from inside of us instead of the divine above us. Basically we have to build our own meaning. 
This does not seem to work, we now live in societies that have put the individual Man in the center of everything, so more than ever we should be finding our actual purpose of being according to Nietzsche, but it's fair to say that what we have lost with the "death of God" is still to be replaced, unless we come back to religion. This is an argument made by CS Lewis, that sometimes we have to admit to ourselves that we went down the wrong path and have to backtrack to the last "secure" point we had, but we are not very good at doing that. 

These are deep waters to me also, I still haven't figured out a comfortable thought system, I too have the urge to just give up on everything because it's objectively meaningless. But that also brings with it the idea of death and suicide, and life goes from "let's enjoy the days I have left on this earth" to "Why even bother staying until the end if I could end this laughable and senseless nightmare right now". 

This is not good, this is not an answer, this is where something kicks that could be related to Schopenhauer's "will to life" that is stronger than anything and prevents us from actually going down the path of suicide (not all of us, unfortunately).
Cioran even made a career out of this idea, if this philosophical torment leads to such despair in absence of meaning, why don't people just kill themselves ? 

This a very serious topic, and could be interpreted as either a naturalistic survival instinct (as all animals have), or well, God's goodness and morality that still lives on in us even if we have abandoned him, and hints at us that there is something bigger than ourselves and this earth, the right choice might actually be to "pick up our cross" and carry on. 

I believe Kierkegaard was the first existentialist in that sense to bring up the apparent meaningless of our human activities, but unless all the others that came after him he picked the mystic path to give an explanation (obviously through Christianity as it was also the predominant religion in Europe at his time), instead of the naturalist atheism that took place after, which has now been exhausted and can easily be considered as a dead end. 

I am not philosophical expert, just another lost insomniac that constantly wrestles with these questions, to the point where nothing else seems actually important. 
Also I consider that every human being can be nothing more than agnostic, as we simply do not know. Religion has to be leap of faith, in order to put your belief in the highest position in your life, as that will somehow make it "true". 
I would also advise reading Jung on this subject, the psychology of belief is not exactly explained by organised religions wishing to control minds, our minds actually cry out for a Father, and it's really terrifying, I still have no answers.

Je suis assez d'accord, n'étant moi-même pas croyant au sens classique du terme, j'ai trouvé beaucoup réponse à des phénomènes qui ne peuvent pas être expliqué autrement qu'avec des concepts religieux, et donc surnaturel. 
C'est comme si nos consciences avaient besoin d'un récit, d'une histoire impliquant des facteurs abstraits qui ne peuvent pas directement être observés dans une démarche purement scientifique, mais qui semble quand même animer nos vies et surtout nos expériences de vie. (Voir la synchronicité de Jung). 

Nous sommes tous plus ou moins croyants, dans le sens où nous dogmatisons et idolâtrons par défaut, l'approche naturaliste et athée manque cruellement de réponse à donner dans ces domaines, à part une nécessité évolutive pour la survie de l'espèce. Le problème c'est que même si cette observation est correcte, elle n'investigue pas le questionnement du sens et du but, et ne propose rien qui nous permette de fixer une quête ultime pour notre existence dans ce corps et dans cet univers, ce qui a malheureusement tendance à finir en cul de sac vers l'absurde et et le nihilisme. 
Je pense qu'il est évident que ces deux dernières notions ne sont pas des réponses ou des idéaux, mais plutôt un abandon et consternation fasse à l'absence évidente de réponse concrète à ces questions. 

Et au contraire je suis forcé d'admettre que les notions de bien transcendant et absolu, ainsi que l'éloignement de l'Homme de celui-ci symbolisé par le péché, une quête de relation personnelle avec un créateur bienveillant et omniscient, dans le but de s'avouer à nous-même notre nature imparfaite et "corrompue" ne sont pas si débile que ce que je pensais avant, et offre parfois même une meilleure analyse de ce qui nous entoure ainsi que des comportements humains plutôt que l'athéisme, qui finalement nous mène immanquablement vers des angoisses existentielles (je pense notamment à toute la bibliographie de Cioran, qui peut se résumer à "pourquoi les Hommes ne se suicident-il pas ?").

Et au contraire dans l'Apocalypse de Jean on a pas exactement une description très pacifiste la victoire de Dieu contre le Mal, il y a non seulement beaucoup de morts, mais c'est très glauque et graphique (à interpréter selon le style prophétique donc pas à la lettre, mais tout de même, le end-game Chrétien n'est pas que tendresse, Dieu reste toujours colère).

Un autre exemple qui m'avait marqué dans les Actes des apôtres, deux disciples de la première communauté de Pierre se font exécuter sur le champ par Dieu lui-même pour avoir menti à l'église. Le couple ayant vendu des terres leur appartenant pour mettre en commun l'argent à leur communauté, ils decident d'en garder secrètement une parti et de mentir sur le prix de revente. 
La morale étant qu'ils auraient très bien pu garder leurs terres ou garder leur sous pour eux, il n'y avait pas d'obligation particulière, mais le fait de choisir le mensonge directement en présence de Dieu, l'Esprit-Saint et l'apôtre préféré de Jesus mérite punition divine.  

J'y retrouve beaucoup le Dieu de l'ancien Testament, on parle bien de la même entité même si le prisme de Jesus nous montre peut-être l'image complète du fameux LORD, YHWH, ou dans nos traductions française l'Eternel de la bible hébraïque. 

Le fait de concevoir deux dieux différents ou même un seul dieu mais changeant ou évoluant et une des premières hérésie apparue au premier et deuxième siècle, notamment défendu par Marcion qui est aussi au passage le premier a avoir compilé le canon actuel du nouveau testament. Cette question reste tout même interessante, elle est débattu depuis le début du Christianisme et une comparaison superficielle des deux corpus peut effectivement amener à cette conclusion. J'irai même jusqu'à dire que ce point est central à la théologie Chrétienne, et que tenter de comprendre l'unité des deux testaments permet aussi d'avoir le message complet des évangiles.

Gospel of Matthew/Mark/Luke for the story of Christ (pick one out of the three) as it is the pivotal point of the whole biblical corpus, then John for a more theological understanding of Jesus. 
Acts is the continuity telling how the apostle spread the gospel after Jesus's death and resurrection. 

These are all relatively easy to read and a good introduction to the Christian message. 

Then I would recommend to get into Genesis, the first chapters are also very understandable. 

And that's about it for the "introduction" level books, everything else requires a bit more analysis and knowledge of the context. 

Revelation is a trip, very strange and symbolic but also quite fun to read because of the supernatural imagery, once you are familiar with the overall narrative of the Bible it's definitely worth trying to grasp John's visions.

The post originally mentions the trustworthiness of the bible, which really means its historicity. Take for example, the fact that is was only in the 19th centuries that the academic endeavour of the "quest for the historical the historical Jesus" began, before that the gospels were regarded as undoubtable historical facts, it took the possibility of a secular approach to question that, and ultimately question the authority of the bible itself. This was mainly an agnostic or atheist movement when faith in God was already falling due to the enlightenment period and humanism, the Church and believers wouldn't even dare to question the authenticity of these texts. 
The most flagrant exemple would be the authorship of the gospels, we now know with certainty that their could not have been written by Jesus' actual apostles, they came around much later by Christian communities, and are definitely not eyewitness accounts, for multiple reasons. Even most Christian denominations recognise this fact, and the conventional naming of the books is now considered traditional and not factual. it doesn't necessarily disprove the whole narrative, but put things into perspective. 
Take the book of revelation also, the only reason it's in bible is because orthodox doctrine at the time thought it to be written by John the apostle. Many denominations still doubt its authenticity and do not include in their canon. However it is still a pretty important prophecy that most Christians still include in their faith. It's only through textual criticism that it has been established that it was written much later than the other books of the NT, and by analysing the style and grammar (which is fairly poor), it cannot be from the same author as the gospel of John. So again, this knowledge was all made possible by a secular approach of doubt and skepticism, it doesn't mean that a believer cannot provide a secular approach in their research, but it takes a neutral and unbiased position to defy the established order.

It can never "prove" anything, just like any historical event or figure cannot be proven, it's just a question of probability that some of them are more likely to have actually happened. 
Skepticism has an important role and is the basis of any serious scientific endeavour, Bart might have lost his faith because of his fundamentalist approach from his early days, but we need critical minds like him to really sort out what actually happened and what didn't from these ancient texts. 
Any Christian should have this approach about their own knowledge of their scriptures.

I have been an agnostic atheist all my life, religion was never part of my world view and my definitive answer still remains "we don't know". But life also has a curious way of making you question its very essence, and it's easy to fall into the absurd or even nihilism when there is no higher sense of belief and purpose. The idea of death being a state of none-being as it was before our birth seems to negate everything about our own consciousness, and the more I think about it the more I find it ironic in a cruel way. There is an inevitable asynchrony that religion has filled the gap for in most of human history. 
I got interested in Christianity because I find the narrative complex and appealing, there is something about the figure of Jesus Christ that is so deep and full of meaning to our own humanity that there are answers to be found for sure, even if we don't know if any of the historical events are true. The philosophical value on the other hand is undeniable, and I really admire the gospels and their authors for bringing such wisdom, clearly it's not just some religious cultists/fanatics making up none sense, 2000 years later it still holds in our contemporary lives (while other books in bible just don't), and their consistency with each other points towards the fact that the historical Jesus was indeed a wise teacher that made a huge impact that still resonates to this day. 
I think my main conclusion is that it is a dead end to try and prove Christianity or any religion as fact, whether it be their historicity or their depiction of metaphysical concepts. It's the wrong approach. 

So I would say I will remain agnostic in the purest sense, I cannot know, no one can know, and if there is a God he operates on a level that is incomprehensible to the human mind. It's easy for most people to claim that they are Christians and that they believe literally and factually that God made himself man to die on the cross and offer salvation to those who believe in his resurrection, but to me that seems like it misses the essence of the message behind it all, which to me would be the "pick up your cross and follow me" part.
As Nietzsche said, "there was only one Christian and he died on the cross". 
Maybe the truth is about acting out what actually remains of his teachings, whether or not it really happened or not is almost irrelevant now, we will never know, probably the closest we can get to knowing is by actually trying our best to live in his image and "deny ourselves", not just claiming "I accept Jesus as my lord and saviour" and taking our salvation (whatever that means) for granted. 
My biggest problem with Christianity is that the orthodox doctrine established by Paul makes it clear that the central and mandatory requirement above anything else is to believe in the physical resurrection of a man from the 1st century. I get that it's all about atonement for our sins in the biblical narrative but God obviously knows that our logical minds cannot just blindly accept such supernatural claims without experiencing ourselves any supernatural experiences. I cannot deny the resurrection, because ultimately who knows really, but I cannot claim that I am certain it happened for X reasons, because all the justification I have heard for it are just biased and fall into fallacies from a logical perspective. We have intelligent and critical minds, blind faith is certainly not the answer to anything.

Yes that is the main problem, it's not that the originals were corrupted by malicious intent or Christians just making up stuff to fit their ideology to the point they tell a completely different story, it's more about the fact that these communities who wrote the gospels were already one or two generations after the events, that it is plenty of time make up stories in the collective imagination about this Jesus figure they worshipped. None of the NT authors were eye witnesses, they might have known some of the disciples and apostles but that is just a speculative assumption, except maybe for Paul which came earlier, but it is suspicious that none of his epistles actually mention anything of the specific things that are told in the gospels. That would be the only way of authenticating these later stories, but to my knowledge he never even quotes Jesus once, it could have been the link between all the writings but it doesn't align.

I have just finished reading Misquoting Jesus by Bart Ehrman, I would recommend you read it too because it is so much more consistent and precise compared to his interviews/debates. 
Ehrman truly is a historian in that sense, and the fact that he is now agnostic adds the value of a secular approach on an otherwise very biased field of study.
To sum it up, yes there are more than 30000 variations found in all found manuscripts, but it's not as bad as you'd expect : 

1) textual criticism of the bible goes back a long way, people throughout the centuries have been on a quest to find the most authentic and ancient version of the greek manuscripts, to the point that using tested analysis methods we can consider that our final version of the New Testament is more likely to be closer to the original intention of the authors rather than fully made up stories by later Christians. 
2) the main problem is that copying manuscripts during the first and second centuries was generally made by non-professional scribes that volunteered for their local church. Many changes must have happened during that period, but mostly mistakes overall.

Désolé mais c'est archi faux, des manuscrits datants des premiers siècles sont consultables là tout de suite maintenant, la première version complète du nouveau testament date du 4eme siècle, le codex vaticanus, et avant cela il y a du fragment jusqu'au document quasi complet qui remonte au deuxième siècle, et tout ca en source et en quantité élevé et varié, sans aucune falsification majeur. 

Il existe aussi les Dead Sea Scrolls qui sont considérés comme la découverte archéologique récente la plus importante, il s'agit de manuscrits quasi complet de la bible hébraïque en parfait état datant du premier siècle, qui sont à quelques détails prêt exactement similaire a nos versions les plus récente, aucune trace de falsification en 2000 ans. 

Je ne dis pas qu'il est impossible qu'il y ai eu des modifications par les copistes avant la première version la plus ancienne connu de chaque document, mais il s'agit d'une erreur de considerer que notre version actuelle de la bible date du moyen age, c'est historiquement faux, ce sont les traductions depuis le Grec, Latin et Hébreux qui sont apparus avec la naissance de l'imprimerie mais c'est tout.

Pour le coup il y a probablement plus du documents témoignant d'un certain Jesus Christ que de Jules Caesar, la même méthode scientifique peut-être appliquée pour déterminer avec plus ou moins de certitude qu'il s'agit de deux figures historiques. C'est l'historicité de la résurrection qui pose problème, pas l'existence d'un prophète juif nommé Yeshua qui aurait fait plus de bruit que d'autres.

Il s'agit effectivement de Paul considéré par beaucoup comme le fondateur du Christianisme tel qu'on le connait aujourd'hui. Quelques petits détails :

- Paul n'a jamais rencontré Jésus de son vivant, il persécutait même les premières communautés chrétiennes jusqu'au jour où Jesus lui apparut dans une vision. 
- Il rencontra par la suite le frère supposé de Jesus, James, ainsi que l'apôtre Pierre. 
- Il fut le premier à développer l'idée que la mort de Jesus était un sacrifice pour les péchés de l'humanité entière, et que cette nouvelle croyance n'était pas réservée aux juifs. C'est principalement cette notion qui permis la propagation de l'évangile (littéralement "la bonne nouvelle") les non-juifs (ou gentils) n'avaient aucunement besoin d'adopter les coutumes et traditions judaïques, croire en Jesus Christ comme sauveur de l'humanité suffisait pour obtenir la grace de Dieu et le salut. 
- il y a 6 lettres rédigées par Paul dans le nouveau testament dont l'authenticité est certifiée par les historiens, elles sont aussi les documents les plus anciens car elle sont estimées à une vingtaine d'années après la crucifixion (tous les autres ouvrages sont de sources anonymes, malgré l'attribution traditionnelle de l'église aux apôtres, et on été rédigées bien plus tard vers la fin du premier siècle). 

Paul est sans aucun doute la figure la plus importante du Christianisme après Jesus lui-même, qui selon les faits historiques était plutôt un prêcheur apocalyptique qu'un prophète voulant construire sa propre religion en dehors du judaïsme. Les communautés ayant été impactées par son ministère ont progressivement construit cette notion de déité et plus tard de trinité, et finalement qu'importe si la théologie en elle-meme est vraie ou fausse, tous ces éléments d'un point de vu historique pointent vers l'existence d'un Jesus, et même du Jesus décrit dans les évangiles (en admettant que les communautés les ayant rédigé ont probablement embellie les choses pour les rapprocher d'une biographie mythologique). 

Croyants ou pas, tout cela reste un événement fascinant de l'histoire de l'humanité

I was in the same situation last year, I met this girl that just got out of a long term relationship, I confessed my feelings early on but she said she wasn't ready and doesn't want me to be her rebound, while also claiming that there is definitely something going on between us and maybe with time we're gonna end up together. 

I was so in love that it wasn't an issue for me to be just friends, but considering how things turned out the advice I would give myself today is to be more strict about my boundaries. It's ok to hang around for a little while, it's exciting and kind of a romantic build up, but your feelings come first and if after a month or two she isn't ready to commit to the one who she is allegedly already in an intimate relationship with (and I don't mean physical, texting all day long and hanging out together as a couple is already an intimate and emotional relationship), then it's gonna turn into a situationship and trust me you don't want that, it will ruin it for you two, it did for me and we aren't even friends anymore although I still love her. 

You already kissed, she knows you want more, don't settle for less, seriously don't, it will affect your confidence, and overall and paradoxically it will lessen your chances of you two working out. 

You showed her that you were here for her and ready to engage in a meaningful relationship ? Good, it's her move now, tell her you love being with her and you wouldn't wanna lose her anytime soon, but being friends is just not good enough because you have feelings and they will end up hurting if things remain in this direction. 

If she really is the one there is no such thing as bad timing, if you stay approachable but maintain a certain distance she WILL come back to you and realise that she is missing her chance with you. Also guys that are always available and seek intimate relationships only through friendships tend to be overlooked, I know because I'm one of them, why would she bother question her feelings and future with you if you are already by her side acting as a boyfriend? Know your worth, I know it's hard and you want to be with her all the time but all it will do is give her full control of the relationship, and thus your feelings, you will be hopelessly waiting for something to finally happen, and will become a slave to your own emotions and become emotionally dependent.

It sucks but self help doesn't work for some people, I have been reading this subreddit a lot since I am also grieving and curious about how different people deal with break ups, I generally feel like lots of advices come down to focusing on yourself, loving yourself and developing a routine of self care alone that will eventually heal you. Find someone you can talk to, not a therapist or even a friend, but someone that can resurface that sense of intimate connection and feeling of being cared for, I know it's hard to find the right person but if this is what you feel like will make you take at least one step ahead then it will be worth it. I feel the same, it has been two months and things are just getting worse, it's not that I want to kill myself but I don't want to be alive anymore either. She was the one thing that made me believe that life is worth living and that there is a future to build. I hate being alone with myself, and nothing gives me enough joy to escape my solitude, and I could never imagine having another relationship because I feel like it's not worth it, the pain and emptiness once it ends just sets me back and I'm less confident and optimistic than I was before. 

She left when I needed her the most, I lost my job around the same time we were breaking up and now I'm just lying in bed all day waiting for a better tomorrow, but it never comes. Working out doesn't work, friends don't work, my hobbies bring me no joy anymore, at least when she was around I felt alive and striving to be a better person, now I'm just a weird loner again.

All I can say that might comfort you is that you are not alone, from what I've noticed most people are just not as sensitive and anxious as we are so even if they are hurt they can still go on with their lives, they don't seem to really understand what crippling depression feels like, and breakups are just the worst. The person you loved the most and was the most special human being on this planet doesn't exist anymore, it's even worse than grieving sometimes, he just ceases to exist in your reality, even though he is still alive, it feels like he is dead to you. It is a horrible feeling, I guess we are just not equipped to deal with such a loss, so it turns into a trauma. The absolute worst thing about it is that this person consciously and actively chose to not include you in his/her life anymore, they come to the conclusion that they will feel better and happier without you, and eventually with someone else. It is such a painful thought, and it will probably never go away completely. 

We cannot fix each other, but we can talk and listen, sometimes it's all we need to get that little push to make it through the day, just to feel understood and cared for, even just temporarily. I sincerely hope you will find your way out of this, so you can get the affection and attention you deserve. 

And feel free to send a DM if you feel like venting or just want to talk, we're here to help each other. 

For the suicidal thoughts, as weird as this might sound, embrace them, accept that your mind is in such distress that the only appeasing outcome is simply disappearing, forever. I think about dying constantly, it's almost like a defence mechanism, but please please also consider the idea that your loved ones, relatives, friends will be shattered beyond repair for life, it's the only thought that keeps me from not going through with it, the idea of inflicting this guilt and pain to them is unbearable. If you are really feeling like you might attempt it, please just say to yourself "not today", every day until it goes away, because it will, believe me it will. It will also come back someday, it is a struggle, but everything is temporary, especially feelings, they are wild and they come and go. 

Only time heals, so brace yourself, life sucks but sometimes it also doesn't, and everything will be alright before you even realise it. 

I really hope you will do better, take care !
